title: The test suite runs in minutes on Windows
goal: A change runs only the checks it can break, and on the project's Windows 11 host python3 _tools/tests.py finishes within the Windows ceiling of _tools/tests_ceiling.json with nothing else running, and kb-tests-windows finishes within its job timeout.
notes: Baseline of the old suite on the project's Windows 11 host (i7-8665U, 4 cores/8 threads, NTFS, Defender real-time protection on, no exclusions): tests.py 1,106-1,203 s wall for 1,134 tests on 8 workers, 55% of worker time in fixture setup; kb/_self/reports/test-suite-speed.md holds every number with its command. Time sinks, largest first: (1) every fresh kb tree pays about 15-19 s of first-open cost for its new files, most likely Defender's synchronous scan on open (a hard-linked copy 0.4 s); (2) every fresh clone rebuilds the pack index cold (12.8 s for the first rag.py pack, 14.5 s for the first check.py); (3) process starts: about 1,044 python and 6,920 git children per run, 2-3 minutes of worker time. The CI jobs are manual: a pipeline status is not a gate result, the local gate is. Retitled 2026-10-06 as the operator's answer to ST-f2gtof46 gate g2 (retitle) says: the 'no lost coverage' clause and the stress suite went with the test cut, and the ceiling file holds the run-time bound; the suite it measured is gone (53 ids), so the sinks above are the premise of its open stories, not current figures. Its open stories stay for the operator to keep or drop (ST-4mcoplex, ST-xjb4wykm; ST-b3bbbbpc carries gate g2 on that).
